words.sense: A force or event that sets an action in motion or speeds its progress.
misconceptions: Mistaking a conditional future benefit for a past catalyst.
Ignoring whether the motivating force is an event or something to gain.

words.sense: An offered or expected benefit that motivates a choice or effort.
misconceptions: Treating any trigger that gets action started as a promised reward.
Ignoring whether the motivating force is an event or something to gain.

semantic_axes.description: Impetus is the push that starts or accelerates action, whereas an incentive is a prospective benefit offered to encourage it.

chains.frame: Which word best describes the storm’s role in Beatriz’s repair campaign?

beats.text: After heavy rain washed away part of the cycle path, Beatriz finally started collecting signatures for repairs.
beats.reason: A damaging storm triggered action. A force or event that sets an action in motion or speeds its progress.

beats.text: She had discussed the problem for months without acting before the storm.
beats.decisive_clue: months of delay show that the event supplied the push
beats.reason: Months of delay show that the event supplied the push. A force or event that sets an action in motion or speeds its progress.

chains.feedback_short: Months of delay show that the event supplied the push.
chains.feedback_deep: Impetus means a force or event that sets an action in motion or speeds its progress; incentive means an offered or expected benefit that motivates a choice or effort. Here, a damaging storm triggered action. The new detail does not change the deciding fact: months of delay show that the event supplied the push. Thus impetus remains the stronger choice.
chains.contrast_rule: Impetus sparks action; an incentive gives you something to gain.

hints.attention: Focus on what made her move from talking to acting.

hints.contrast: Impetus sparks action; an incentive gives you something to gain.
